mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which negatively impacts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent decline in real estate sales (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4.5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE is below 4.5% and PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals robust economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 increases for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, it signals inflationary pressure and potential monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS > 4%
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% and FEDFUNDS is above 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month signals weakening consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS decreases by more than 1% in a month.
